Title: Diagnosis of test `testSingleOptionSingleArgument`
Details:
The failing test `testSingleOptionSingleArgument` shows a failure in the assertion on line 70:
```java
assertEquals("[" + enteredValue1 + ", 1000]", b + "");
```
Here, the test expects the list `b` (obtained by `cmd.getValues("-b")`) to contain, in order, `enteredValue1` and then `1000`.

The test constructs a parser using `createDefaultValueParser(new String[]{"100", "1000"})`, then parses an argument array `{"-b", "1"}`, and after parsing expects the option `-b` to have values `[1, 1000]`.

We inspected the parsing mechanism in `Parser.parse(String[] arguments)`:
- It creates a mutable list from the input arguments.
- It creates a `WriteableCommandLine` and processes the group options iteratively to parse arguments.
- It applies defaults from the model before processing.
- After processing all possible options, it validates the command line.

We looked at `CommandLineImpl.getValues(String)` which delegates to `getValues(Option, List)` with an empty list default.

The test failure suggests the second default value `"1000"` is expected to be present after the explicitly set argument `"1"` when retrieving the option values. This indicates:
- The default value setting on the option is not being properly applied or merged with the explicitly given argument during parsing.
- Alternatively, the `getValues` method might not correctly combine explicit and default values.

Thus, the bug likely arises because default values are not correctly added or retained alongside the explicitly passed arguments during parsing and retrieval of option values.

The suspect code areas are:

- `Parser.parse(String[])`: to verify if defaults are correctly added before, during, or after parsing.
- The method that sets default values on options or command line (`group.defaults(commandLine)`).
- `CommandLineImpl.getValues(...)` to confirm it merges explicit and default values as expected.

Suggested fix locations to investigate and potentially fix:

org.apache.commons.cli2.Parser.parse(java.lang.String[])
org.apache.commons.cli2.OptionGroup.defaults(org.apache.commons.cli2.WriteableCommandLine)
org.apache.commons.cli2.commandline.CommandLineImpl.getValues(java.lang.String)
